source.display_title: 05/07/2026 - Soneel Raj & Farooq Bey KFS- Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session — Lost

call.sequence_note: Second of TWO separate sales calls contained in this single recording file, running 00:56:14 to 01:21:41. This prospect is not named in the file title, which names only the first prospect. Not a follow-up — this is a first conversation with a different person.

setter.evidence: The KFS suffix in the file title belongs to the first call in this recording (Soneel Raj), not to this one. This prospect described coming directly from an Instagram advert and named no setter: 'Well, I was, I just saw the exercise on Instagram.'

prospect.name: Engin Oytac
prospect.aka: Joined first as 'Engin's iPhone', then from a laptop as 'enginoytac' — same person, device change mid-call
prospect.occupation: Tech entrepreneur and small business owner; describes himself as sitting down a lot
prospect.family_status: Married; wife cooks and eats with him. Has sons — at least one at college and into weightlifting; the family has a home gym downstairs.
prospect.training_background: Was a fit water polo player when young; describes becoming sedentary after turning 40. For the past month to six weeks has walked 5 km five times a week, taking an hour to ninety minutes, and reports feeling good on it. Was a serious swimmer — built from 40 laps to 70 laps of a 25-metre pool — until a back injury ended it. Has tried weightlifting at home and dislikes it: 'every time I try, I feel stressed... I feel angry.' Bought a kettlebell after seeing Instagram content and has done the movements with dumbbells; found it energising. Home gym available and unused.
prospect.medical: Sleep apnea, recently started on a device. A back injury from swimming that he describes as worsening — 'my back is getting worse... then my back's got bad, really bad. I hurt my back' — which ended swimming entirely. Weight 118 kg at 5'11", roughly BMI 36. Reports afternoon sugar cravings satisfied with bread and honey, which the rep attributed to insulin and blood sugar. Drinks alcohol around three times a week, recently reduced.

signals: Self-describes the loss and its start point: 'I used to be really fit in healthy, younger ages, but then after turning 40 I kind of became lazy. So now I need to kind of pick it up again.'
Wants a former self back — a water polo player who was 'always natural' and never had to work at fitness

Diverges from the classic rebuilder on regret, which is almost entirely absent: 'nothing bad. I just see the fact that I'm overweight and that I'm getting old, but I'm happy and present, so it doesn't hurt me at all'

Strong secondary read is skeptical_bargain_hunter and it should be considered on review: he is self-directed, his own free walking programme is currently working, he opened by asking whether he could do this from YouTube, he anchored at $100-200 per month, and he left to go and find an app
Frames the decision in startup terms — 'your new startup should be your body, not a new idea' — which is optimizer language attached to a deconditioned body

goals.text: Lose weight — named as the primary objective
Get moving after years of being stationary
Build a consistent routine of three to four workouts a week alongside the walking
Live long — 'if I want to live long, I probably should work out and start getting back on track'
Learn correct movement so he does not injure himself — named as the key criterion
Find a form of training he actually enjoys, after weightlifting made him feel angry and worse
Get his afternoon sugar cravings under control
Make his body the priority for the first time, having always put business and children first

pains.text: 118 kg at 5'11", roughly 60-70 lb above a healthy range, and describes himself simply as overweight
Back injury from swimming that is getting worse and ended the one activity he enjoyed and excelled at
Sleep apnea, only recently on a device
Weightlifting makes him feel stressed, angry and worse rather than better
Sedentary for over ten years since turning 40; health was never a priority behind business and children
Afternoon sugar cravings resolved with bread and honey
Alcohol several times a week, which he identifies as the main dietary issue and does not intend to give up
Has never found the right support — 'I haven't found the right support for me'
A previous online membership bought for his son was, in his words, not helpful at all
Has a home gym and complete flexibility of time and still does not train

objections.raw_quote: Well, yeah, that's out of my range. That's, I mean, I wish you guys, I think on your website, you should actually write those prices, because it's just too much for me. I mean, if it was 100, 200 bucks a month, something we can handle, but that's right now, it's not within our budget.
objections.rep_response: Ran the isolation question — 'Putting the investment aside for a second, do you feel like you actually want to do this?' — and then asked what his plan would be from here. No payment plan was offered, no financial picture was taken, and no other move ran.

objections.raw_quote: the first question in my mind is, you know, can I do this with, just by watching YouTube and just, you know, getting those movements in there. Um. That's the first, you know, the critical mind steps in.
objections.rep_response: Did not answer it. The prospect partly answered it himself ('I think it will be good to work with someone, especially making sure that the movements are right') and the rep moved straight to pricing.

objections.raw_quote: we did use a membership for my son, where one of them was actually online, like this was not helpful at all. But the other one was very helpful. So it just depends on the program.
objections.rep_response: No response; proceeded to present the four price levels.

evidence: Immediate and unambiguous refusal on price: 'that's out of my range... it's just too much for me... it's not within our budget'
Stated a substitute plan on the call: 'I'll just look for apps or other options, and then try to get a more reasonable price'
Rep accepted and closed out: 'Listen, man, we're always going to be here, so I wish you the best'
No payment, no link, no deposit, no follow-up call booked and no next step of any kind
Counter-evidence: intent was genuine — 'I do want to do this' — and he had already bought a kettlebell and started a walking routine unprompted
Counter-evidence: he had said pre-price 'I'll give it a try and see how it goes, if the price is within the range of what I can pay', so the objection was flagged before the number landed
outcome.next_step: None. Prospect leaving to find a lower-cost app or alternative.

notable.note: The clinical picture here is the finding. The prospect disclosed sleep apnea newly managed with a device, a back injury he described as getting worse and which had ended his swimming, and a body mass around 118 kg at 5'11". None of it was asked about and the back injury drew not a single follow-up question. He also stated that his own key criterion was 'making sure that the movements are right, I'm not injuring myself. That's the key' — and that concern was never answered before the price was presented. Two secondary points: this is the first call in the batch where the $1,200 'love it or leave it' product was presented as a standard fourth tier rather than as an exception the rep is not meant to offer, which is the fourth distinct framing of that product in two days; and having run the complete open-wallet financial interrogation on a prospect in bankruptcy the previous day, the rep here asked a business owner not one financial question and released him inside forty seconds of the price objection.

quality.notes: Continuous inversion, including most of the rep's pillar delivery appearing under the prospect's label. Roles resolved from content. The prospect appears under two labels — 'Engin's iPhone' at 00:56:14 then 'enginoytac' from 00:56:36 — because he rejoined from a laptop; both are the same person. This call shares a recording file with an unrelated earlier call and is not named in the file title, so it will be missed by any process keyed on titles or on one-call-per-file assumptions.
